meta.title: Goertzel algorithm: single-bin detection and DTMF
meta.tools: Goertzel recursion (second-order IIR per bin, run with scipy.signal.lfilter), comparison with FFT bins, DTMF decoder, timing crossover
meta.summary: Implement the Goertzel algorithm, show it computes exactly one DFT bin, decode noisy DTMF telephone digits with eight Goertzel filters, and measure how many bins you can compute before a full FFT becomes cheaper.
meta.problem: A touch-tone decoder only needs 8 frequencies. Why compute an FFT of all of them?
meta.theory:
Goertzel: $s[n]=x[n]+2\cos(2πk/N)s[n-1]-s[n-2]$, then $X_k=e^{j2πk/N}s[N-1]-s[N-2]$ — exactly the DFT bin, at N real multiply-adds per bin. A full FFT costs ≈ N log₂N; so Goertzel wins for
K ≲ log₂N bins (≈ 8 for N = 205, the classic DTMF block at 8 kHz). DTMF: rows 697/770/852/941 Hz, columns 1209/1336/1477/1633 Hz.
meta.method:
Exactness: 1000 random (N, k) cases vs numpy.fft. DTMF: 16 digits × 200 trials at SNR 0…20 dB, N = 205, detection = strongest row + strongest column bin (with a twist/threshold check).
Timing: K Goertzel filters (lfilter, C) vs one rfft, N = 205 and 4096.
